title: Cost calculation for the whole chat session
body_excerpt: closed Jan 17 2024 via PR #1269 ("Add usage summary for agents") by Contributor @sonichi -- closure addresses observability portion BUT architectural cost amplification explicitly admitted unsolvable without rewriting GroupChat. RENUMBERED FROM ORIGINAL PASTE (was "ATGN-010" in user paste; ID collision with existing ATGN-010 #4835 prompted renumber to next free ATGN-018). Filed Dec 27 2023 by @stephanedebove tagged enhancement. POWERFUL MAINTAINER-CONFIRMED ARCHITECTURAL COST AMPLIFICATION: Member @afourney Dec 28 2023 quotable: "Group chat is tricky because many messages are duplicated (and thus only need to be counted once), and because there is a hidden OAI call for orchestration that does not show up as a message. At present the entire history is passed to all agents, and is also passed to OAI when doing orchestration. The costs are super-linear -- long chats are much much more costly than short chats. You can mitigate this by using the round_robin... but then the orchestration is basically a simple loop with no llm calls at all. There is no way to mitigate this short of rewriting GroupChat." THIS SINGLE QUOTE DOCUMENTS THREE DISTINCT MECHANISMS: (1) hidden OAI orchestration call cost-not-surfaced; (2) entire history broadcast to all agents = M-context-amplification at delegation layer; (3) super-linear-cost-vs-length-of-chat. Reporter explicit user-impact framing: "is no way to know the cost for a whole CustomGroupChat() session?" + "ways to mitigate the OpenAI costs during a group chat session?" + architectural question "do agents receive the whole history of conversation when they are called?" PR #1269 addressed observability (token tracking summary) but NOT the architectural amplification. Pattern: closed-as-completed-but-architectural-issue-remains. NEW closure sub-shape (11th in taxonomy): closed-by-fixing-adjacent-issue-while-architectural-issue-remains-acknowledged-unsolvable. FOUNDATION ROW FOR M-DELEGATION-FANOUT cluster: maintainer-confirmed architectural cost amplification at GroupChat layer. Tag note: bu chosen over fr because the substantive content is the maintainer admission of unfixed mechanism, not the closed-completed observability portion. Filing-to-close: 21 days for observability fix; architectural cost-amp explicitly unsolved at fetch. [v23 IRR adjudication: retagged bu->fr per second-rater agreement; original tag bu by Sajjad, codebook v1.1 will tighten bu/fr boundary on interrogative-feature-gap titles.]

title: Support approximate token counting for image blocks in langchain-core
body_excerpt: with REPORTER-SHIPPED-FIX-PR-MERGED-FAST pattern. Filed Jan 25 2026 by @subhashyadavon tagged feature + external + core. CLOSED Jan 27 2026 by Collaborator @ccurme via PR #34883 (2 DAYS filing-to-merge -- ties CRAI-011 as fastest in catalog with different mechanism shape). Reporter cost-impact paper-quotable: "If the default approximate counter is used, a single base64-encoded image can appear to consume 25,000+ tokens simply because of its string length, causing trim_messages to aggressively discard virtually all other conversation history." Reporter framework-architectural-mechanism: "Currently, when count_tokens_approximately encounters a message with a list of content blocks (standard for multimodal models), it falls back to len(repr(message.content)). For messages containing base64-encoded images, this results in counting tens of thousands of characters as if they were text tokens, leading to massive overestimation of the token count." Reporter user-impact-on-context-management: "Currently, I have to work around this by either stripping images from my trimming logic or implementing a custom token counter." Source-line: libs/core/langchain_core/messages/utils.py count_tokens_approximately function. Proposed fix: iterate content blocks, identify image_url blocks, apply fixed 85-token penalty (aligned with OpenAI low-res base penalty) instead of counting characters. REPORTER-SHIPPED-FIX-WITH-VERIFICATION-EVIDENCE: "I have already implemented this fix in a local fork, verified it with a new test suite handling 100k+ character base64 strings, and ensured zero regressions by running the existing 141 message utility tests. I am ready to submit the PR as soon as this is reviewed." NEW PATTERN: REPORTER-PREPARED-PR-SUPERSEDED-BY-DRIVE-BY-CONTRIBUTOR. @jiaming2li Jan 26 2026 (1 day post-filing) actually opened PR #34883 -- drive-by contributor shipped fix BEFORE reporter could submit theirs. Reporter prepared-fork was superseded. @ccurme Jan 27 2026 merged. Sub-mechanism: M-multimodal-cost-amplification token-counter-overestimates-via-base64-string-length. DUAL-PATH PROOF for M-multimodal-cost-amplification: LANG-035 (no fix, ~5-month auto-stale-close in 2024) + LANG-036 (2-day fast fix in 2026). 18-MONTH GAP between same-mechanism reports demonstrates mechanism-known-but-unaddressed-until-community-pressure pattern -- the count_tokens_approximately bug existed for entire LANG-035 base64-amplification window (Jul 2024 onward) but only got fixed when (a) reporter framed it as feature-not-bug AND (b) reporter-prepared-PR demonstrated zero-regression on 141 existing tests. Methodology-relevant: framing-and-evidence-quality drives fix outcome, not bug-severity.

title: maxOutputTokens quits agentic loop if max output tokens reached at a particular step
body_excerpt: UPGRADED from SKIPPED in v22-batch-26 revision per codebook section 10. Original triage skipped as S5 (user-found-existing-feature) but new evidence-deepening (Discord-source verbatim quotes, trace evidence, primitive-exists-but-only-via-callback-closure sub-mechanism framing) recharacterizes as fr-shape M-budget-primitive-missing case. CLOSED Dec 31 2025 by Member @roaminro as completed -- via stopWhen-callback workaround NOT first-class config field. Filed Dec 19 2025 by @daneatmastra (Mastra Contributor, Discord-sync-bot mirroring user post). REPORTER ORIGINAL DISCORD-SOURCED QUOTE (verbatim from @arielweinberger Dec 18 Discord post 1451303997465166167): "We have an agentic loop with maxSteps 20. We also have agent.stream(..., { modelSettings: { maxOutputTokens: 5000 } }... we see in our traces that one of the steps reached its output token limit... my understanding is that this setting is at the LLM request level (stop). we have found no way to limit the total output tokens for the entire agentic loop, is there one? That would be our preferred option over setting it at the modelSettings level." CONCRETE TRACE EVIDENCE: stepIndex 3 hit outputTokens 5000 with finishReason: length AND inputTokens: 1 (only 1 input token in iter 3 means this is mid-loop continuation). MAINTAINER WORKAROUND VIA STOPWHEN-CALLBACK NOT FIRST-CLASS CONFIG: @roaminro (Member) Dec 19 (via Discord, mirrored Dec 20 to issue) provided stopWhen callback closure -- "For a loop level limiter, you could maybe use stopWhen, something like this: stopWhen: ({ steps }) => { const totalOutputTokens = steps.reduce((sum, step) => sum + (step.usage.outputTokens || 0), 0); return totalOutputTokens >= 100000; }". Reporter @arielweinberger Dec 19 acknowledgement: "okay, we have not tried that. that seems like the solution." MULTI-USER INTEREST: @suhas_deshpande Dec 18 Discord: "Also curious about this." DISCORD-AS-SOURCE-OF-TRUTH PATTERN: All technical exchange happened on Discord (channel 1309558646228779139); issue is Discord-mirror via daneatmastra automated sync. Documents Mastra primary support venue (Discord) being where actual problem-solving happens, with issues serving as artifact-only mirrors. POST-CLOSURE 7-WEEK-LATER FOLLOW-UP COMMIT: @mathemusician Feb 23 2026 commit e2f8649 "Increase maxOutputTokens to 8000 to fix truncation issue" -- separate-but-related (default cap too low for many use cases). NEW SUB-MECHANISM within M-budget-primitive-missing: primitive-exists-but-only-via-callback-closure (Mastra has stopWhen primitive that CAN do aggregate-budget-enforcement via user-written reduce + threshold-check, but no declarative maxTotalOutputTokens config field at agent.stream() level -- requires user to write closure correctly each time, error-prone vs first-class field). Distinct from SMAG-005 primitive-doesnt-exist, MAST-004 primitive-only-runs-at-memory-retrieval, CRAI-011 primitive-exists-but-broken-via-silent-regression. REVISION TRANSPARENCY NOTE: original S5 skip was correct on narrow reading; updated retention reflects evidence-deepening. Methodology trail preserved.

title: Automatic tool budget reminders via ToolReturn.content
body_excerpt: STRONGEST SINGLE QUOTE IN ARCHAEOLOGY EFFORT. OPEN at fetch tagged feature + capability-solveable. Filed Feb 19 2026 by @sarth6 (Contributor). PAPER-QUOTABLE OPENING SENTENCE: "UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=N) is a kill switch. The model has no idea it is running low on tool calls until the hard cap fires UsageLimitExceeded and the entire run dies, often after the model already did useful work." CONCRETE BATCH-REJECTION-CLIFF EVIDENCE: "The hard cap checks at batch level. check_before_tool_call computes current + batch_size and rejects the entire batch if it would exceed the limit. Model requests 10 parallel calls with a limit of 6 -> all 10 rejected, zero execute." Reporter provides 3 detailed workarounds with each failure-mode characterized: (1) Dynamic @agent.instructions reading ctx.usage.tool_calls -- "puts the budget count in the wrong place. instructions maps to system_instruction in the Google API and {role: system} in OpenAI. That is the top of the context, before the model has read through any of the conversation history containing those tool calls. It is like putting page 8 of 10 in the header of page 1." + busts prompt cache; (2) tool return value pollution -- "pollutes the tool return schema. Instead of getting [...] directly, the model has to dig into {results: [...], remaining_budget: 5}. Every consumer of the tool type has to unwrap the wrapper"; (3) Manual ToolReturn.content -- "right position in the conversation. But it requires every tool author to manually track call counts, compute remaining budget, and format the reminder. If you have 5 tools, you are writing the same bookkeeping code 5 times." MAINTAINER ACTIVE ENGAGEMENT: Member @adtyavrdhn Feb 19 proposed @agent.on_tool_results hook abstraction. Collaborator @DouweM Mar 5: "This sounds like a good candidate for a hooks-based Capability once #2885 lands as part of #4303." Member @adtyavrdhn Mar 5: "Yep once middleware capabilities lands we will be able to close off a lot of these in one go." Reporter @sarth6 Mar 5 acknowledged: "Sounds good, I will work on a temporary package for now with the goal of deprecating it once that launches." AUTHOR-SHIPPED-EXTERNAL-PACKAGE: @sarth6 Mar 5 commit ff82bf9 + Mar 11 published pypi.org/project/pydantic-ai-tool-budget. External-package-as-de-facto-fix pattern at n=3 (parallels SMAG-002 + LANG-028). Cross-references: PR #3691 ToolPolicy + issue #2593 (tool_calls_limit recently merged) + issue #843 (closed original limit-tool-calls request). PROMOTIONAL-COMMENT-PATTERN at n=3: @fjnunezp75 Mar 15 GPU-Bridge service spam (after MAST-017 Agenium + CRAI-011 agentic-qa-api). Sub-mechanism within M-budget-primitive-missing: primitive-exists-but-only-as-hard-cliff-without-graceful-degradation-or-budget-awareness. Cross-ref to OAAS-002 same batch confirming SAME architectural pattern in OpenAI Agents SDK -- DUAL-PATH PROOF for hard-cliff-without-graceful-degradation variant. title: Agent memory/history consolidation after a number of interactions
body_excerpt: OPEN at fetch (13+ months) despite multiple PRs in flight and active community engagement. Filed Mar 6 2025 by @nikos-kal tagged enhancement. EXPLICIT COST FRAMING: "The management of memory, thus context size, is important because it translates limitations in terms of cost, speed, model choice etc. Other agentic LLM applications like Claude Code deal with this by summarizing the context every few steps or remembering only a limited history." Reporter cited Claude Code architecture as reference. Reporter Mar 10 self-discovered PARTIAL WORKAROUND via step_callbacks (existing feature can do post-step cleanup but not first-class memory_size config). MULTIPLE COMMUNITY PROPOSALS: @Symbolk (Contributor) Mar 17 2025 suggested mem0 integration; @nikos-kal Mar 18 countered: "We still need an easy memory_size configuration in smolagents though because even if you switch to mem0, smolagents would still internally keep their own memory." @ChristianWeyer Mar 26 2025: "So, pluggable memory is on the way @nikos-kal?" -- waiting on resolution. FORK-BASED IMPLEMENTATION PATTERN: @joaopauloschuler (Contributor) Mar 11 2026 implemented in own fork: "In my own fork, I implemented it" -- fork-based-implementation-not-merged-upstream signal-class (NEW closure sub-shape, distinct from LANG-022 stuck-open-with-multiple-PRs because here contributor does not attempt upstream merge). RECENT PRs: @agent-morrow Mar 29 2026 cross-referenced #2129; @saslifat-gif Apr 3 2026 PR #2153 "feat: add max_context_chars parameter for automatic memory truncation." Sub-mechanism: M-context-amplification at agent-step-loop runtime level. DISTINCT FROM DSPY-001/DSPY-003 (optimizer-compile-time amplification at MIPROv2 batch-summary and bootstrap-demo steps respectively) -- here it is runtime-iteration-amplification at MultiStepAgent.run() level. ESTABLISHES M-CONTEXT-AMPLIFICATION AT TWO ARCHITECTURAL LEVELS: compile-time (DSPy optimizers) AND runtime (smolagents agent steps). Cluster expands from dspy-architecture-specific (n=2) to architecture-class with 2 sub-classes (n=3 across 2 frameworks).

title: Is there a step timeout feature?
body_excerpt: OPEN at fetch tagged bug. Filed Apr 2 2025 by @forest-snow with concrete benchmark context: Haiku 3.5 (code agent) on smolagents benchmark MATH subset using LiteLLM and Bedrock, "often take much time because the model may write a brute-force code snippet and it takes a while to execute a step (>500 seconds)." REPORTER EXPLICIT GAP-IN-EXISTING-CONTROLS: "While there is a MAX OPERATIONS for the local python executor, it did not seem to help fix this issue." -- MAX_OPERATIONS counts AST operations not wall-clock time, leaving wall-clock-runaway uncontrolled. ACTIVE MAINTAINER ENGAGEMENT: @aymeric-roucher (Collaborator) Apr 4 2025 asked for minimal repro isolated to python executor: "Could you provide a code snippet that involves, not the full agent and LLM, but only the python executor with the faulty code?" COMMUNITY CONFIRMATION 4 months later: @heckfy88 Aug 22 2025 confirmed mechanism with concrete repro suggestion: "it is the default LocalPythonExecutor, it does not have a timeout arg, so every tool call is limited by, I think, 300s, after that is timeout exception. To reproduce it just call a tool that has time.sleep(1000)." @coderabbitai 3 weeks before fetch cross-referenced langflow PR #12713. Sub-mechanism: per-step-wall-clock-runaway during code execution. CLASSIFICATION NOTE: candidate cluster fit is contested. Original triage assigned to M-retry-loop as wall-clock variant. Alternative classification: this fits with MAST-014 (OM observer-LLM blocking 148s, ephemeral-token-counting) as wall-clock-amplification-inside-agent-loop -- distinct mechanism class from HTTP-retry-on-error (LANG-024/025/026/027 + MAST-007/016 are all HTTP-retry mechanisms; SMAG-004 is Python-executor wall-clock). Candidate new cluster M-execution-time-runaway with MAST-014 (n=2 across 2 frameworks, below codebook section 10 n=3 threshold to elevate to own M-category in v1.1). For v23 retention: classify as wall-clock-amplification-candidate, do not absorb into M-retry-loop. [v23 IRR adjudication: retagged bu->fr per second-rater agreement; original tag bu by Sajjad, codebook v1.1 will tighten bu/fr boundary on interrogative-feature-gap titles.]
